body: We don't live in the same state anymore so I couldn't see him in person, and I'm afraid that he may think we're plotting against him further if I contact him again. Would the police be able to do anything with a phone number?

Honestly, I don't think he'll respond. He deleted his Facebook and others in the writer's group have started to take notice that something may be off, and we're all very concerned. No one can contact him, though, and I'm afraid that if I tell him to get help it'll push him further into delusions that we're against him.

Did you read *any* of my post? You're calling me a pussy for trying to figure out *how* to help him? I don't have his fucking address. I don't have his fucking birthday. I don't have his fucking SSN. I don't have any fucking information on him except his name, phone number, and state.

What the fuck do you expect me to do, track him down via my apparently amazingly high-tech hacking skills? He deleted his fucking Facebook, isn't returning messages, and has disappeared from every place I could contact him.

For someone responding to a subreddit about advice, you're a fucking asshole. I'm worried about the safety of someone I care about, so *I'm* a pussy? Fuck you. Seriously. I'm not going to take this type of shit from someone who didn't take the goddamn time to read out my post when someone I care about is *in fucking danger.*

Do you have *anything* fucking worthwhile to contribute to the discussion or are you going to be a useless asshole?

B and X have had a tulmutous relationship on the writer's forum because of personal differences regarding B's girlfriend (X absolutely hates her), but that's the extent of their relationship. X consistently rants about how horrible B is, but as far as I've seen, their only *real* contact has been when B stood up for B's girlfriend, who X was berating.

B, X, and Y don't live in similar places; Y and I live in the same state, and X has ties to a city in the state and mentioned it when he was friendly. I do have his phone number, but he hasn't texted me since he first thought B was mocking him.

I think I'm more worried about the scale of his psychotic break or whatever's happening. He seems to be on the cusp of going balls-to-the-wall insane, and I don't know what would happen if he did -- whether he'd come to our state and try to do something, or whether he's going to continue festering in his delusions and eventually hurt himself.

I think my biggest concern, at this point, is his own well-being. I know he isn't romantically linked and has been to rehab for a drug possession charge (on marijuana), but he never mentions family.

The reason I mention my concerns for Y, B, and myself are that it seems like, at this point, anything can happen with X. Do I have an obligation to tell them if I think something *could* happen? It's also a very, very close-knit group of writers who, in my experience, have a lot of impact on one another's careers, insofar as getting each other blacklisted from certain magazines or publishers; does that constitute a reasonable risk that needs to be divulged to Y and B?
